callouts.label: Tummy Signal
callouts.hint: The child notices a softly rumbling stomach before eating.
callouts.description: A growling or empty-feeling stomach can be one hunger signal.
callouts.ap_tip: No single signal appears the same way for everyone.

callouts.label: Energy and Focus Signal
callouts.hint: The same child feels low energy and distracted at a desk.
callouts.description: Hunger may show as lower energy, headache, irritability, or difficulty concentrating.
callouts.ap_tip: These clues can also have other causes, so check the whole situation.

callouts.label: Check What the Body Needs
callouts.hint: Icon-only thoughts show water, rest, feelings, play, and food.
callouts.description: A pause can distinguish hunger from thirst, tiredness, boredom, or emotion.
callouts.ap_tip: Different needs can happen at the same time.

callouts.label: Begin Eating with Attention
callouts.hint: The child starts a varied meal calmly.
callouts.description: Attention to taste, smell, and body comfort makes internal signals easier to notice.
callouts.ap_tip: There is no required pace or perfect meal.

callouts.label: Pause During the Meal
callouts.hint: The utensil rests while the child checks comfort.
callouts.description: A midway pause is information, not a rule to stop.
callouts.ap_tip: Ask: Has hunger changed? Does eating still feel comfortable?

callouts.label: Hunger Decreases
callouts.hint: A downward gauge and relaxed expression show hunger becoming gentler.
callouts.description: Hunger usually shifts gradually as food is eaten.
callouts.ap_tip: Signals can change before the plate is empty.

callouts.label: Comfortable Fullness
callouts.hint: The child leans back comfortably with relaxed shoulders.
callouts.description: Comfortable fullness may feel satisfied, steady, and no longer interested in more food.
callouts.ap_tip: Fullness is not the same as painful overstuffing.

callouts.label: Outside Prompt
callouts.hint: A screen, package, or peer offer appears beside the child.
callouts.description: Large packages, screens, schedules, and social cues can influence eating even when body signals differ.
callouts.ap_tip: Notice the prompt without blaming yourself.

callouts.label: Reflect After Eating
callouts.hint: The child notices steady energy and comfort after the meal.
callouts.description: Reflection can help connect choices with wellbeing over time.
callouts.ap_tip: The goal is curiosity, not judging the amount eaten.
